Over the same period, average town-wide use fell by 7 percent during unusually wet weather. Volunteers were not randomly selected and may have been more motivated to save water. Twenty participants installed new appliances during the pilot, but the report did not separate their results. The proposed expansion costs $18 per household per year and would initially reach 2,000 homes. The contractor describes the difference between 11 and 7 percentage points as the program’s “proven impact.” The council’s access officer notes that some residents share meters, some do not have email and some cannot control leaks in rented homes. The contractor offers printed reports at an additional cost that has not yet been estimated. Landlords already receive maintenance notices, but the council has not linked them to the display pilot. A residents’ group supports conservation while opposing comparisons that could shame larger households or people with disability-related water needs. The council must choose between full expansion, a revised pilot or ending the project. It has enough funds for the quoted digital service but has not approved a print budget.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Contractor: The displays clearly made people more responsible. A four-point improvement is a result any council would welcome. Access officer: It may be promising, but we haven't isolated the display from weather, motivation or new appliances. And “responsible” is a loaded description when someone cannot fix their landlord’s leak. Council member: Would you remove comparisons altogether? Access officer: I would start with a household’s own pattern, explain limits and offer a way to report problems they cannot control. We should test whether the message helps people act. Resident: I would read a paper report, but I don't want a league table of my neighbors. Please don't spend the whole budget before finding out who can actually use the service.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Числа и процентные пункты переданы точно.
Утверждение о причинности ограничено дизайном пилота.
Решение учитывает разные возможности действовать.
Предложены ясные данные для следующего решения.

tasks.prompt: Evaluate the “proven impact” claim, calculate the quoted annual expansion cost and name two excluded or underserved groups.
tasks.model: The quoted digital cost is $36,000 a year. The four-percentage-point difference is not a proven causal effect because selection, weather and appliance changes are not controlled. People without email, shared-meter users and renters unable to repair leaks may be underserved.
tasks.explanation: 11% − 7% = 4 процентных пункта, но арифметическая разница не является доказанным эффектом.

tasks.prompt: Explain why “more responsible” is challenged and how the officer’s proposal differs from removing all comparison.
tasks.model: It makes a moral judgment about behavior people may not control. The officer proposes comparison with a household’s own pattern, clear limits and a route to report uncontrollable problems, rather than abolishing useful feedback.
tasks.explanation: Определи оценочную нагрузку слова responsible и восстанови предложенную середину.

tasks.prompt: Write a 220–280-word recommendation to the council. Choose a course, assess the evidence, address access and privacy, and specify what the next decision needs to know. Include the known cost and an unknown cost.
tasks.model: I recommend a revised pilot before committing to full expansion. The reported reduction among volunteers is promising, but the contractor’s claim of proven impact goes beyond the evidence. Town-wide use also fell during wet weather, participants selected themselves, and appliance replacements were not analyzed separately. The four-percentage-point difference therefore cannot be treated as the display’s isolated effect. The quoted digital expansion would cost $36,000 annually for 2,000 homes. That figure excludes printed reports, whose cost is still unknown. A revised design should test whether residents understand and can act on the information, including people without email, households sharing meters and renters dependent on landlords for repairs. Comparisons should focus on a household’s own pattern, with explanations for circumstances that change demand. Public rankings would risk shaming residents without establishing what they can control. Reports should provide a clear route for maintenance concerns and explain who receives the data. Before the next decision, the council needs an access plan with print costs, separate information about appliance changes, and a more credible comparison strategy that accounts for weather and participant differences. The pilot should also record whether reported leaks lead to action and whether residents can use the proposed reporting route without additional help. If wider access proves unaffordable, the council should narrow the service transparently rather than describe a digital-only system as universal.
tasks.explanation: Выбор полного развёртывания или отказа тоже возможен при аргументах; модель показывает соразмерный путь до новых доказательств.

tasks.prompt: Respond to: “You are delaying conservation because the evidence is imperfect.” Explain your threshold and propose a time-bounded step. Then: “Can we fund print by removing maintenance support?” Negotiate the tradeoff and request missing information.
tasks.model: We can continue helping residents conserve water while testing the claims more carefully. A revised pilot with a fixed review date would let us check access before scaling. I would not remove maintenance support without knowing how many renters cannot act otherwise. What would print cost, and could we target paper reports to residents who need them?
tasks.explanation: Нужна позиция с действием, а не требование абсолютной научной уверенности.

tasks.prompt: Explain the proposal in Russian for tenants, then give the contractor one neutral English correction to its marketing claim.
tasks.model: Предлагается доработать испытание, чтобы проверить пользу, стоимость бумажных отчётов и возможности людей без доступа к счётчику или ремонту. Снижение расхода заметили, но влияние самой рассылки не доказано. Людей не следует публично ранжировать по расходу. The pilot showed a larger reduction among participating households, but it did not isolate a causal effect of the displays.
tasks.explanation: Точная коррекция сохраняет положительный наблюдаемый результат без недоказанной причинности.

transfer.prompt: A voluntary electricity-alert pilot reports an 8% fall while the city falls 5%; heat-pump installations differ and tenants lack thermostat control. Write a new recommendation and a plain-language claim the supplier could honestly publish.
transfer.model: I would revise the pilot to examine installation changes and whether tenants can act on the alerts. The observed difference is encouraging but does not establish causation. An honest claim is: participating homes used less electricity during the pilot, but further evaluation is needed to determine how much the alerts contributed.
transfer.explanation: Новый ресурс и механизм контроля требуют переноса принципа доступного действия.

units.reflectionPrompt: Перепиши рекомендацию, исправив две наиболее существенные слабости. По-русски объясни одну правку причинного вывода и одну правку для конкретной группы жителей.

units.title: Проверка: справедливая процедура найма
units.why: Сопоставь эффективность, опыт кандидатов и неполные показатели, затем договорись об улучшении процесса.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text: A fictional software company replaced open-ended interviews with a timed take-home exercise for junior applicants. The task was advertised as taking two hours and was scored using a common checklist. Recruiters report that interview scheduling time fell by 40 percent. Of 60 candidates invited to complete the exercise, 38 submitted it; the previous interview round had 52 attendees out of 60 invitees. The applicant groups were different, so the difference cannot be assigned entirely to the new task. Several candidates said the exercise took five hours, especially when they polished the presentation. The scoring checklist rewarded completeness, readability and a working solution, but candidates saw only the broad instruction “show us your best work.” One hiring manager argues that extra effort demonstrates commitment. Another worries that unpaid time disadvantages people with jobs or caring responsibilities. No analysis of later job performance has been completed. The company has hired eight people through the process, too few for confident conclusions about long-term retention. Candidates can request accommodations by emailing the recruiter, but the invitation does not explain what adjustments are possible. The team must redesign the next round in two weeks without adding more than thirty minutes of recruiter time per candidate.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Recruiter: The task has made our lives easier, but I can't say whether the missing candidates were weaker or simply busier. Manager: We still need to see independent work. Candidate adviser: Then tell people what “good enough” looks like and stop rewarding invisible extra hours. Manager: If we publish the checklist, won't everyone just optimize for it? Adviser: If the checklist measures what matters, that's a feature. If presentation polish is not part of the junior role, don't let it silently decide the score. Recruiter: Could we use a shorter draft plus a structured fifteen-minute discussion? Adviser: Possibly, as long as the discussion has consistent questions and an accessible alternative. We need to test the actual time with people outside the team.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Различаются удобство работодателя и качество отбора.
Критерии связаны с реальной задачей.
План укладывается в ресурс и срок.
Коммуникация уважает приватность и не обещает доказанную справедливость.

tasks.prompt: Compare employer time saved with candidate participation and explain why neither proves better hiring. Identify one mismatch between instructions and scoring.
tasks.model: Scheduling time fell, but only 38 of 60 candidates submitted, compared with 52 of 60 attending previously. Different groups prevent a simple causal conclusion, and later job performance has not been analyzed. Candidates were told to show their best work without seeing the completeness/readability criteria or a clear stopping point.
tasks.explanation: Скорость процесса, участие и качество найма — три разные величины.

tasks.prompt: Explain the adviser’s response to “optimizing for the checklist” and the condition attached to a short discussion.
tasks.model: If the checklist measures relevant job skills, knowing it helps candidates focus appropriately. A discussion needs consistent questions and an accessible alternative so that it does not reintroduce arbitrary judgment.
tasks.explanation: Не вся оптимизация является обманом; значение зависит от качества критерия.

tasks.prompt: Write a 220–280-word redesign proposal. Keep independent work, address hidden time and accommodations, fit the recruiter limit and state how you would evaluate the next round without claiming proven fairness.
tasks.model: I recommend a short independent draft followed by a structured fifteen-minute discussion. The invitation should publish the scoring criteria, explain what a sufficient draft includes and explicitly state that extra presentation polish will not earn additional credit unless it reflects a relevant job requirement. Before launch, people outside the hiring team should try the exercise so its advertised time is credible. Candidates should receive examples of available adjustments and a private contact route, with an equivalent accessible alternative to the discussion. The same core questions and scoring guidance should apply across interviews, while allowing clarification of a candidate’s own work. This preserves independent problem-solving and uses only fifteen minutes of the additional thirty-minute recruiter allowance, leaving the rest for consistent administration and accommodation arrangements. The current evidence shows lower scheduling time, not better hiring. The previous round had 52 interview attendees among 60 invitees; in the new round, 38 of 60 invitees submitted the task. These are different participation measures in different applicant groups, and we do not know why people withdrew. In the next round, we should collect optional reasons for withdrawal, actual task-time reports and candidate understanding of the instructions. We should also review scoring consistency and, over time, relevant job performance. These checks can reveal problems; they do not justify labeling the redesigned process fully fair before it has been tested.
tasks.explanation: Числа старого и нового процесса должны быть подписаны; альтернативные планы допустимы в пределах дополнительного времени.

tasks.prompt: Answer: “People who really want the job will find five hours.” Challenge the inference respectfully. Then: “We only have two weeks.” Negotiate a minimum viable change and identify what must wait for evidence.
tasks.model: Extra unpaid time may reflect someone’s circumstances rather than motivation or ability. We can still assess independent work with a clear stopping point. Within two weeks, I would prioritize publishing the criteria, testing the task duration and standardizing a short discussion. Longer-term job-performance analysis will need to continue after this round.
tasks.explanation: Вежливое несогласие оспаривает связь между временем и мотивацией, а не личность менеджера.

tasks.prompt: Write a Russian candidate-facing explanation of the proposed process and an English manager briefing. Do not promise a particular accommodation or reveal candidates’ private circumstances.
tasks.model: Предлагается короткое самостоятельное задание с открытыми критериями и структурированное обсуждение. Доработка оформления сверх требований не должна приносить скрытый бонус. В приглашении планируют объяснить доступные варианты адаптации и личный канал запроса; конкретные условия ещё нужно согласовать. The redesign preserves independent work while making expectations and time costs explicit. Its fairness and predictive value still require evaluation.
tasks.explanation: Слово proposed должно сохраняться при смене аудитории.

transfer.prompt: A scholarship asks for an “optional” video but reviewers favor polished videos; applicants have unequal equipment access. Design a replacement with a clear criterion, an equivalent format and a plan to check whether the change improves access.
transfer.model: Define the skill being assessed before choosing a format. If the aim is explaining a project, accept equivalent written or simple audio responses and score clarity of reasoning rather than production quality. State that optional material carries no hidden advantage. Review participation and applicant feedback across formats, while avoiding a premature claim that the redesign eliminates every barrier.
transfer.explanation: Ситуация требует распознать скрытый критерий и предложить эквивалентность, а не просто сократить часы.

units.reflectionPrompt: Перепиши предложение после разбора. По-русски назови скрытое допущение, которое убрал, улучшенную формулировку критерия и то, что пока нельзя проверить по имеющимся данным.

units.title: Составить решение о финансировании
units.why: Синтезируй разные стандарты доказательности и скрытые институциональные интересы в рекомендации для правления.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text: The North Harbor Arts Fund has $90,000 to allocate between an established theater’s outreach program and a new network of neighborhood workshops. The theater requests $70,000 to continue school performances and subsidized tickets. Its evaluation reports 3,200 attendances, a 92 percent satisfaction score among questionnaire respondents and testimonials from teachers. It does not report how many distinct pupils attended or whether schools that declined the offer faced transport barriers. The theater has an experienced finance team and can submit quarterly reports. The neighborhood network requests $55,000 for six workshop sites, translation, childcare and paid local coordinators. It has run two small pilots, attended by 74 people in total. Interviews suggest that participants valued meeting neighbors and having a role in choosing activities, but follow-up is incomplete. The network has not previously managed a grant of this size. Its budget includes administrative training, which one board member describes as money “not reaching participants.” The fund’s current scoring system gives equal weight to reach, evidence of impact, financial reliability and alignment with its mission to widen cultural participation. Applications do not define reach consistently. The theater counts each visit; the network counts individuals once. A consultant proposes selecting the theater because its figures are stronger and its reporting capacity reduces risk. Another adviser argues that repeatedly funding organizations already able to produce polished evidence may prevent new groups from developing. The fund cannot fully finance both requests. Either applicant could submit a smaller scope, but neither has yet stated what it could responsibly remove. The board must also consider continuity: schools have provisionally reserved theater dates, while workshop coordinators have delayed other work pending the decision. Neither applicant has been promised funding. The fund publishes its reasons, including conditions and any departure from its scoring approach. It wants a decision that can withstand scrutiny from unsuccessful applicants as well as supporters.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Chair: We are not choosing between art and community. Both applications serve the mission, but in different ways. Finance trustee: I agree, although the established theater can demonstrate delivery. Asking us to fund administrative training sounds like asking us to buy the network’s ability to receive our money. Community trustee: Or it is paying for the infrastructure we quietly assume established organizations already have. Program officer: The network’s small scale is a real limitation, but it is also why attendance totals alone would predetermine the result. Consultant: We still need a decision rule. We cannot solve structural inequality through a grant decision that becomes impossible to monitor. Chair: Could we invite reduced proposals with a common definition of reach and a proportionate reporting plan? Finance trustee: Only if that does not become an informal promise to split the award. Program officer: And we should not demand a controlled impact study from a six-site pilot while accepting satisfaction surveys as impact evidence from the theater. Chair: Then the request needs to explain what we can compare now, what remains uncertain and which risks we are prepared to carry.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Несопоставимые показатели выявлены и заменены разумным основанием сравнения.
Риторический эффект отделён от приписывания мотивов.
Рекомендация содержит решение, условия и публичное обоснование.
Регистр меняется по аудитории без потери существенных оговорок.

tasks.prompt: Analyze how definitions, evaluation methods and administrative capacity affect the apparent strength of the bids. Identify a defensible comparison and one comparison the data do not permit.
tasks.model: The theater’s attendances cannot be directly compared with the network’s distinct individuals. Satisfaction among respondents and incomplete interviews are both limited indicators, not equivalent causal impact measures. Administrative capacity offers evidence about grant management but may also reflect previous access to funding. The board can compare documented delivery and budget requirements while asking for a shared reach definition; it cannot infer that the theater produces greater social impact from its larger total alone.
tasks.explanation: C1 требует связать техническую проблему показателя с институциональным следствием, сохраняя реальный риск неопытности.

tasks.prompt: Explain the competing implications of “buy the network’s ability to receive our money,” and identify the safeguards trustees attach to a revised-proposal process.
tasks.model: The phrase frames training as overhead serving the fund rather than participants. The community trustee reframes it as necessary infrastructure whose cost is hidden in established organizations. Revised proposals must use comparable definitions and proportionate monitoring without implying a promised split or applying tougher evidence standards to the new group.
tasks.explanation: Риторический анализ не требует приписывать говорящему недобросовестный мотив; объясни эффект формулировки.

tasks.prompt: Write a 300–380-word board recommendation. State an immediate decision, justify fair comparison, specify what reduced bids must include, explain acceptable risk and provide publishable reasons without promising either applicant funding.
tasks.model: I recommend requesting time-limited reduced proposals from both applicants before allocating the award, while making clear that this is an information-gathering stage and not a commitment to divide the fund. The present figures do not support a simple ranking of impact: the theater counts attendances, the network counts individuals, and neither evaluation isolates the program’s wider effects. The theater nevertheless offers credible evidence of delivery and established financial controls. The network offers a plausible route to participation through translation, childcare and local decision-making, alongside genuine management risks. A fair process should acknowledge both features rather than treating polished reporting as impact or inexperience as a benefit in itself. Each reduced proposal should identify the minimum viable scope, consequences of removing activities, distinct participant estimates and barriers that may exclude people. Applicants should also state existing commitments accurately, distinguishing provisional reservations from contractual obligations. Reporting requirements should be proportionate to the award: the theater should clarify unique reach and participation barriers, while the network should explain financial oversight, coordinator support and how administrative training will protect delivery. For either award, monitoring should combine financial accountability with evidence of who participates and what they experience. The board should explicitly decide which risks it can carry. Staged payments and a defined review point could make limited support for the network manageable; they should not be presented as proof that its program will succeed. Equally, continuity at the theater is relevant but does not create an entitlement from dates booked before a funding promise. Published reasons should explain the mission tradeoff, the limitations of the evidence and any conditions attached to the eventual award. If reduced bids show that only one can operate responsibly within the available funds, the board should say so plainly. A process that is open about its uncertainty is more defensible than a numerical ranking built on incompatible measures.
tasks.explanation: Рекомендация не обязана выбирать отсрочку, но должна дать немедленное действие, критерий решения и понятное объяснение проигравшему заявителю.

tasks.prompt: Record a board exchange. Trustee: “Your fairness argument makes reliability sound like a disadvantage.” Clarify the distinction and defend a decision rule. Applicant: “You asked us to revise; surely that means we will receive something.” Repair the expectation without becoming dismissive, then check understanding.
tasks.model: Reliability should count as reliability; the problem is allowing it to stand in for every other criterion. I propose comparing viable scope, participation barriers and proportionate controls, then making the remaining mission tradeoff explicit. To the applicant: we requested a revision because we need to understand your minimum viable program, not because an award has been agreed. I recognize the work that involves. Would a clear deadline and a list of the unresolved criteria help you decide how to respond?
tasks.explanation: Профессиональный тон соединяет точную границу обещания с признанием издержек адресата.

tasks.prompt: Write a Russian explanation for workshop participants and a concise English paragraph for the public decision record. Preserve the distinction between administrative cost and waste, and between invitations and awards.
tasks.model: Правление пока предлагает запросить сокращённые программы; это не обещание денег. Для новой сети обучение управлению может быть условием надёжной работы, а не бесполезной тратой. При этом небольшой опыт действительно создаёт риск, который нужно описать и контролировать. The proposed process would seek comparable, viable proposals before allocating the fund. It would recognize established delivery capacity while assessing how each program widens participation; an invitation to revise would create no funding entitlement.
tasks.explanation: Перевод для участников проще, но не скрывает риска и отсутствия решения.

transfer.prompt: A foundation must choose between a large science museum counting visits and mobile labs counting unique rural pupils. The labs need accounting support; the museum has strong satisfaction surveys but little access data. Write a decision framework and a public explanation that could be read fairly by the unsuccessful bidder.
transfer.model: Use a common reach definition, ask both applicants about barriers and distinguish satisfaction from wider impact. Treat accounting support as a cost to assess against delivery risk, not automatically as waste. Request minimum viable scopes if neither can be funded fully, and explain which mission tradeoff ultimately determines the award. Public reasons should acknowledge the unsuccessful bid’s strengths and avoid presenting an uncertain judgment as a scientifically proven ranking.
transfer.explanation: Новый предмет финансирования проверяет перенос справедливой сопоставимости, а не заучивание названий организаций.

units.reflectionPrompt: Доработай два ключевых абзаца рекомендации и одну устную реплику. По-русски объясни изменения в доказательности, распределении риска и отношениях с адресатом. Укажи, какой довод мог бы изменить твою рекомендацию.

units.title: Подготовить кураторскую интерпретацию
units.why: Удержи неоднозначность исторического свидетельства и сделай её доступной посетителям без ложной нейтральности.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text: A small museum is preparing an exhibition about the former Mill Street factory. Its collection includes a 1964 company brochure, an unsigned letter found in a supervisor’s papers and an oral-history interview recorded in 2019. The brochure describes the factory as “a family with a place for everyone” and shows a picnic, a training room and a newly installed production line. Payroll records indicate that women were concentrated in lower-paid packing roles, while the brochure’s training photographs show only men. The unsigned letter complains that workers who questioned weekend shifts were described as disloyal. The museum cannot establish who wrote it or whether it was sent. In the oral history, former packer Elena Ruiz recalls friendships and a supervisor who helped her arrange shifts around childcare. She also says that promotion “was something other people talked about.” The interview occurred more than fifty years after the events, and Elena asked the interviewer to omit a story involving a named colleague. The museum has permission to use the remaining interview but not the omitted account. A donor whose family managed the factory wants the exhibition to emphasize employment and community life. A workers’ group argues that the “family” metaphor concealed unequal power. The curator wants a label of no more than 220 words beside the brochure and a longer audio introduction. Labels elsewhere in the museum tend to state settled facts, so visitors may interpret an unqualified quotation as the museum’s own judgment. The exhibition budget permits a listening station and large-print text, but no new research trip before opening. Further archival work may be possible afterward. The museum’s collections policy requires it to distinguish documented facts, attributed memories and uncertain provenance. It also requires consent restrictions to remain visible in internal production notes so that later editors do not accidentally restore excluded material.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Donor: My grandfather paid wages when there were few other employers. I don't object to difficult history, but I would hate the exhibition to make him a cartoon villain. Workers’ representative: Nor do we want workers presented only as victims. They built friendships and resisted rules, but that doesn't make the pay structure fair. Curator: Elena’s account seems useful precisely because it holds those things together. Producer: The line about promotion is powerful. Could the actor say it with obvious bitterness? Curator: We should not add an emotion the recording does not establish. We can describe the contrast without performing a verdict for her. Donor: Then what do you do with the unsigned complaint? Curator: Show what it says and what we cannot authenticate. It can raise a question without proving every worker felt the same. Workers’ representative: And don't let the uncertainty about one letter blur what the payroll records actually show. Producer: For the audio, perhaps we explain how visitors can read the brochure as an argument the company made about itself.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Источники сопоставлены с разной степенью уверенности.
Есть ясный интерпретационный аргумент без карикатуры.
Согласие и границы цитирования сохранены.
Сложность адаптирована к посетителю и рабочей команде.

tasks.prompt: Classify one claim from each source by evidential status, and explain why uncertainty about the letter does not make the payroll pattern equally uncertain.
tasks.model: The brochure documents the company’s public self-description, not proof that everyone experienced a family atmosphere. The letter records an unattributed complaint whose authorship and circulation are unknown. Elena’s interview is an attributed retrospective memory. Payroll records document a gendered concentration in lower-paid roles. Uncertainty about one source does not erase independently documented patterns in another.
tasks.explanation: Не переноси неопределённость автоматически с одного источника на всю историю.

tasks.prompt: Explain the shared objection to caricature, the risk in an actor’s “obvious bitterness,” and the proposed way to frame the brochure.
tasks.model: Both sides resist reducing people to simple moral roles. Adding bitterness would impose an emotional interpretation not established by the recording. The brochure can be framed as the company’s argument about itself, inviting visitors to compare it with payroll records and memories.
tasks.explanation: Интерпретация голоса должна опираться на запись; здесь у нас только содержание и прямое замечание куратора.

tasks.prompt: Produce a 170–220-word brochure label and a 130–180-word production note. The label must make one clear interpretive argument while distinguishing sources; the note must protect consent, performance accuracy and accessibility.
tasks.model:
LABEL: “A family with a place for everyone”: this is how the factory described itself in 1964. The brochure’s picnic and training photographs invite viewers to see employment as belonging. Other evidence complicates that invitation. Payroll records show women concentrated in lower-paid packing work, while the training photographs feature only men. Former packer Elena Ruiz, interviewed in 2019, remembered friendships and practical help with childcare. She also recalled that promotion “was something other people talked about.” Her account suggests that support and limited opportunity could coexist, although a later memory cannot reconstruct every worker’s experience. An unsigned complaint describes pressure over weekend shifts. We do not know who wrote it or whether it was sent, so it cannot stand for the workforce as a whole. These sources ask us to examine what the company’s family metaphor made visible and what it left out. The factory provided employment and community; those benefits did not necessarily mean equal access to pay, advancement or the power to disagree. Look at the photographs and the records together before deciding what kind of belonging this brochure offers.

PRODUCTION NOTE: Use only the interview material covered by Elena’s permission. Mark the excluded colleague story clearly in internal records so later edits cannot restore it. If an actor reads the approved words, label the performance as a reading and avoid adding bitterness that the recording does not establish. The unsigned letter needs an explicit provenance note. Keep the payroll finding distinct from the letter’s uncertainty. Provide the complete audio script in large print at the listening station, including source distinctions. Review label and audio together so shortened passages do not turn the company’s quotation into the museum’s own claim. Any future archival findings should be logged and assessed before the interpretation is updated. Do not turn photographs showing only men into proof of a formal rule excluding women from training; the supplied records do not establish that rule.
tasks.explanation: Модель допускает аргумент о власти, но подтверждает его конкретными источниками; производственная записка — другой жанр с действиями.

tasks.prompt: Record replies. Donor: “The word inequality erases the good he did.” Respond without surrendering documented findings. Producer: “Visitors need a simple answer, not source notes.” Negotiate one accessible way to preserve uncertainty.
tasks.model: Recognizing unequal pay and opportunity does not require denying employment or personal support. The label should show how those experiences coexisted. For visitors, we can keep the main argument clear and use short signals such as “payroll records show” and “an unsigned letter claims.” Could we test whether those phrases make the distinction understandable without overloading the label?
tasks.explanation: Сложность можно сделать доступной через краткие сигналы источника, а не через отказ от интерпретации.

tasks.prompt: Give a Russian museum volunteer a 100–150-word explanation of how to answer “Was the factory good or bad?” Add an English reply that invites a visitor to examine a specific source.
tasks.model: На вопрос «Фабрика была хорошей или плохой?» лучше предложить сравнить конкретные свидетельства. Она давала людям работу и дружеские связи; Елена вспоминает помощь с графиком. Одновременно ведомости показывают, что женщины преимущественно занимали хуже оплачиваемые упаковочные должности. На фотографиях обучения видны только мужчины, но сами фотографии ещё не доказывают официального запрета женщинам учиться. Воспоминание Елены соединяет поддержку с ограниченными перспективами продвижения. Автор жалобы неизвестен, и мы не знаем, было ли письмо отправлено: оно не представляет мнение всего коллектива. Не пересказывай исключённую историю о коллеге — разрешения на неё нет. Можно признать неоднозначность памяти, не ставя под сомнение подтверждённые сведения из ведомостей. Предложи посетителю посмотреть, какой образ принадлежности создаёт буклет и что добавляют другие источники. Try comparing the company’s training photographs with the payroll records. What does each source show, and what would we still need to know about access to training?
tasks.explanation: Посредничество предлагает способ рассуждать, не превращая добровольца в носителя окончательного исторического суда.

transfer.prompt: An exhibition on a school has a celebratory brochure, verified exclusion rules and a fond alumni memory. A donor requests an entirely nostalgic tone. Draft a label argument and a response that preserves both memory and documented exclusion without forcing the witness to express emotions absent from their account.
transfer.model: The school’s celebratory image can be read alongside rules that limited who could belong. A former pupil’s affection is evidence of that person’s experience, not a rebuttal of exclusion. I would tell the donor that nostalgia can remain in an attributed voice while the museum explains the documented boundaries of access. A label should invite comparison rather than make the witness perform a judgment they did not express.
transfer.explanation: Новая институция проверяет перенос различения памяти, документа и кураторского голоса.

units.reflectionPrompt: Перепиши наиболее спорное предложение этикетки и ключевой пункт производственной записки. По-русски объясни, как изменились атрибуция, эмоциональная окраска и доступность. Укажи альтернативное прочтение, которое текст должен оставить возможным.

units.title: Проверка: исследование и пресс-релиз
units.why: Отредактируй публичное утверждение так, чтобы оно оставалось полезным, не превосходя возможностей исследования.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text: A university team studied a voluntary four-week lunchtime walking program among office employees. Of 210 people invited, 86 joined and 61 completed both the initial and final questionnaire. Participants reported slightly lower stress at the end. There was no randomly assigned comparison group, and the final week coincided with the completion of a demanding project at one major employer. The researchers measured self-reported stress, not clinical diagnoses or work productivity. Interviews suggest that some participants valued leaving their desks with colleagues; others found the scheduled walk difficult to combine with caring duties or variable lunch breaks. Twelve participants who stopped attending answered a brief follow-up: several cited time pressures, two mentioned mobility barriers and others did not give a reason. The researchers have drafted a paper describing the findings as preliminary and proposing a larger study with a comparison group and more flexible participation. The university communications office proposes the headline “A lunchtime walk cuts workplace stress.” Its draft introduces a participant’s account of feeling calmer and quotes the lead researcher saying that movement and social contact are plausible mechanisms. The researcher did not say which mechanism explains the observed change. A sponsor sells workplace wellbeing services and wants permission to reuse the release. Its promotional draft adds the phrase “a proven route to a more productive workforce.” The university allows partners to quote approved releases but requires separate approval for modified claims. A newspaper reporter needs a 100-word comment by noon. The research team wants a more measured public message without making the study sound worthless. It also wants future recruitment to welcome workers with different mobility needs and schedules, although the next study’s accessible formats have not yet been designed. There is no evidence in the supplied material about medical treatment effects, and the study should not be used to make such claims.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Communications officer: If we lead with “small uncontrolled study,” nobody will read beyond it. Researcher: We don't need to put every limitation in the headline, but “cuts stress” sounds causal. Reporter: So what can I actually say happened? Researcher: People who completed the questionnaires reported lower stress after joining the program. We cannot separate the walks from selection, the end of the project or other changes. Sponsor: But walking and social contact are established good things. Researcher: That does not validate this particular productivity claim, which we did not measure. Officer: What about “Workers report less stress after lunchtime walking pilot”? Researcher: Better, if the article makes the voluntary sample and missing follow-up clear. Reporter: And those who dropped out? Researcher: They matter. A program can be pleasant for those who stay and still be hard for others to access. We should not describe the next study as accessible to everyone before we have worked out the formats.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Точно восстановлены знаменатели и исходы.
Публичное сообщение информативно без причинного преувеличения.
Внутренняя записка содержит выполнимые редакционные действия.
Нюанс сохраняется при смене жанра и языка.

tasks.prompt: Reconstruct the participation funnel and explain three distinct overclaims in the proposed publicity.
tasks.model: Of 210 invited workers, 86 joined and 61 supplied both questionnaires. “Cuts stress” implies causation that the design does not establish. Productivity was not measured, so the sponsor’s claim has no direct support. Universal accessibility cannot be promised before formats are designed. Attrition and a voluntary sample also limit generalization.
tasks.explanation: C1 предполагает различать причинность, измеренный исход и охват, а не свести всё к маленькой выборке.

tasks.prompt: Explain why plausible mechanisms do not validate the sponsor’s statement and why dropout experiences belong in the public account.
tasks.model: A plausible explanation is not evidence that the program caused the observed change or improved an unmeasured outcome. Dropout accounts reveal participation barriers that would be hidden by reporting only the experience of completers.
tasks.explanation: Сохраняй различие plausibility и demonstrated effect.

tasks.prompt: Write a 90–110-word newspaper comment, a 180–240-word internal correction note and a replacement headline. Keep each genre appropriate; specify which sponsor wording must be reapproved.
tasks.model:
HEADLINE: Workers report lower stress after voluntary lunchtime walking pilot.

COMMENT: In a four-week pilot, workers who completed both questionnaires reported slightly lower stress after taking part in lunchtime walks. The finding is encouraging, but the study cannot establish that walking caused the change: participation was voluntary, there was no randomly assigned comparison group, and a demanding work project ended during the study. Productivity and clinical outcomes were not measured. The next research step is to test the program more rigorously and improve participation options. Experiences of people who stopped attending are also important, because time pressures and mobility barriers may limit who can benefit.

INTERNAL NOTE: Replace the causal headline with one that attributes the result to participants’ reports. The main text should state the recruitment and completion figures and explain that the findings are preliminary. Retain the participant’s account as an individual experience, not evidence that every worker will respond similarly. Describe movement and social contact as plausible mechanisms rather than established explanations for this result. The sponsor’s added claim about a proven route to productivity must be removed or submitted for separate approval; the study did not measure productivity, and permission to reuse the approved release does not authorize stronger wording. Ask the sponsor to confirm the final text before publication. The accessibility paragraph should state an intention to develop flexible formats with potential participants. It must not promise universal access before those formats exist. Include what is known about withdrawal while respecting the limited follow-up: twelve former participants replied, so their reasons cannot represent everyone who stopped. These revisions preserve the useful observation and the case for further research while preventing a small exploratory study from carrying claims it was not designed to test.
tasks.explanation: Три жанра выполняют разные действия: заголовок привлекает точно, комментарий объясняет, записка назначает редакционные изменения.

tasks.prompt: Answer a reporter: “Are you saying the study tells us nothing?” State its value and limit. Then answer the sponsor: “Can we just put an asterisk after productive?” Negotiate an acceptable replacement.
tasks.model: The study tells us what participating completers reported and highlights issues worth testing, including access barriers. It does not isolate a causal effect. An asterisk would not repair a headline claim about productivity that was never measured. You could say the pilot found lower self-reported stress among completers, with the study’s limits made clear and the wording approved.
tasks.explanation: Нельзя исправить неподдержанное главное утверждение скрытой сноской.

tasks.prompt: Explain the result in Russian for workplace representatives, then give the sponsor a concise English instruction about reuse.
tasks.model: В небольшом добровольном пилоте у завершивших оба опроса снизился самооценённый стресс. Нельзя отделить прогулки от других изменений, а производительность вообще не измеряли. Причины прекращения участия показывают возможные барьеры, но известны не для всех. Please reuse only the approved wording; any modified claim, especially about productivity, requires separate approval and supporting evidence.
tasks.explanation: Понятное объяснение не превращает исследование в медицинскую рекомендацию.

transfer.prompt: A voluntary reading-break pilot measures self-reported focus but its sponsor claims fewer employee errors. Completion is incomplete and workloads change. Write a public comment and an internal edit rule distinguishing the measured outcome, causal claim and marketing extrapolation.
transfer.model: PUBLIC COMMENT: The pilot measured employees’ own reports of focus. The supplied brief does not give the direction or size of that result, so we should not announce an improvement. Voluntary participation, incomplete follow-up and changing workloads would also limit a causal conclusion. Employee errors were not measured, and the sponsor’s claim goes beyond the reported outcome. INTERNAL EDIT RULE: Check the actual focus results before describing a change. Attribute any result to self-report, state the missing follow-up and avoid causal language unsupported by the design. Remove the error-reduction claim unless separate evidence supports it.
transfer.explanation: Требуется перенос на другой неизмеренный исход, сохраняя структуру доказательности.

units.reflectionPrompt: Доработай публичный комментарий и одну инструкцию спонсору. По-русски объясни, какое ложное впечатление устранил, какие ограничения оставил и почему не перечисляешь все детали в заголовке.

units.title: Проверка: неполная информация и публичное доверие
units.why: Подготовь сообщение об ошибке организации, распределив ответственность без преждевременных обещаний.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text: A regional library network has discovered that an automated reminder system sent overdue notices to 1,400 accounts that had already returned their books. The notices listed book titles, due dates and a standard warning that borrowing could be suspended. The network has confirmed that no accounts were actually suspended by the faulty batch. It has not yet established whether every notice went to the correct email address. The technical team has paused reminders while it reviews address matching and recent software changes. A help-desk spreadsheet contains 86 complaints, including several from people who share household email accounts. These complaints do not establish the total number of people who saw another person’s borrowing information. A vendor’s initial statement calls the incident a “cosmetic messaging error.” The library director wants to apologize promptly but is concerned about suggesting a confirmed disclosure before the review is complete. The communications team proposes saying that “no private information was compromised,” which the technical lead says cannot yet be verified. Branch staff need a script for calls, especially from people worried about titles appearing in a shared inbox. The network can provide a dedicated callback line and place updates on its homepage. It cannot give a reliable completion time for the technical review today, but can commit to another update at noon tomorrow. Staff should not ask callers to read book titles aloud in a public branch queue. The organization’s response team will separately determine any legal reporting duties; your task is to prepare accurate communication from the supplied facts, not advise on those duties. The director has authorized withdrawal of the incorrect notices and confirmation that they will not create fines or suspensions. No decision has been made about compensation or changes to the vendor contract.
materials.source: Авторский вымышленный материал English Workshop, 2026

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Director: I want us to say sorry without sounding as though we know less than the public expects. Technical lead: Pretending we know would be worse. We can say the notices were wrong and confirm that the batch did not suspend accounts. We cannot yet rule out address-matching problems. Branch manager: Callers will ask whether their book choices were exposed. “We are investigating” on its own sounds evasive. Communications officer: Then say what we are checking, what we have done and when we will speak again. Director: Should we repeat the vendor’s “cosmetic” explanation? Branch manager: To someone worried about a shared inbox, that would sound dismissive. Technical lead: It is also premature. We haven't established the scope. Communications officer: The apology should take responsibility for our service, even while the cause is being investigated. We can give staff a private callback route and tell them not to ask for sensitive details in public.
materials.source: Авторский сценарий для синтезированной озвучки English Workshop, 2026

rubric: Известное и неизвестное отделены ясно.
Извинение не перекладывает всю ответственность на поставщика.
Обещания находятся в полномочиях организации.
Скрипт даёт полезное действие и уважает приватность.

tasks.prompt: Separate confirmed facts, open questions and unauthorized promises. Explain why the complaint count cannot establish the disclosure scope.
tasks.model: The notices were wrong, 1,400 accounts were affected and the faulty batch caused no suspensions. Address matching and the extent of any unintended readership remain under review. Compensation and vendor-contract changes are not authorized. Eighty-six complaints are neither all affected accounts nor a count of distinct unintended recipients.
tasks.explanation: Точность требует не смешивать accounts, complaints и people who saw information.

tasks.prompt: Explain why “cosmetic” and an unqualified “we are investigating” both fail, for different reasons. What structure is proposed instead?
tasks.model: “Cosmetic” minimizes a potentially substantive concern before the scope is known. “We are investigating” alone gives no useful account of action or timing. The team proposes confirmed facts, the specific checks underway, immediate protections and a promised update time.
tasks.explanation: Одно выражение переутверждает, другое недоинформирует; различай эти ошибки.

tasks.prompt: Write a 180–230-word public statement and a 120–170-word staff call script. Apologize, withdraw the notices, state what is known and unknown, give next steps and a precise update commitment; avoid legal conclusions or unsupported reassurance.
tasks.model:
PUBLIC STATEMENT: We are sorry that our reminder system sent incorrect overdue notices to 1,400 library accounts whose books had already been returned. We are withdrawing those notices. They will not create fines or suspensions, and we have confirmed that the faulty batch did not suspend any accounts. We have paused automated reminders while our technical team checks address matching and recent software changes. We have not yet established whether every notice reached the correct email address, so we cannot currently rule out unintended access to borrowing information. We understand why this uncertainty is worrying, especially for people using shared household inboxes. Please contact our dedicated callback line if you have a concern; staff will arrange a private conversation rather than ask you to discuss book titles in a public queue. We cannot give a reliable completion time for the technical review today. We will publish another update on our homepage at noon tomorrow, including any confirmed findings and the next steps, even if the review is still underway. We take responsibility for the accuracy of our service and will correct the information we provide as the facts become clearer.

STAFF SCRIPT: I am sorry you received an incorrect notice. The library has withdrawn the affected notices, and they will not create fines or suspensions. We know the faulty batch did not suspend accounts. We are still checking whether every message went to the correct address, so I cannot yet confirm who may have seen borrowing details. You do not need to read book titles aloud here. I can arrange a private callback through our dedicated line. The next public update is at noon tomorrow on the library homepage, even if the investigation is not complete. I cannot promise compensation or a specific technical completion date, but I can record your concern through the private process and explain where the next confirmed update will appear.
tasks.explanation: Извинение признаёт сервисную ответственность, не придумывая вывод об утечке или отсутствии ущерба. Скрипт сохраняет приватность.

tasks.prompt: Reply to a caller: “So you admit everyone saw my books?” Correct the inference empathetically. Then reply to the director: “Can we promise this can never happen again?” Offer a credible commitment instead.
tasks.model: I understand why the uncertainty is upsetting, but we have not established that anyone else saw your notice. We are checking where messages were sent and can discuss your concern privately. I would not promise that no error can ever recur. We can commit to explaining the confirmed cause, the safeguards we introduce and how we check whether they work.
tasks.explanation: Сочувствие не требует подтверждать неверное предположение; обещание процесса лучше недоказуемого абсолютного обещания.

tasks.prompt: Write a Russian explanation for branch volunteers and a two-sentence English correction for the vendor’s draft. Keep the unknown risk visible without presenting it as confirmed.
tasks.model: Ошибочные уведомления отзывают; они не приведут к штрафам и блокировкам. Пока проверяют, все ли письма ушли по верным адресам. Нельзя ни утверждать утечку для каждого читателя, ни обещать, что никто ничего не увидел. Не просите человека называть книги вслух; предложите личный обратный звонок. Please remove “cosmetic messaging error”: the scope has not yet been established. Describe the confirmed incorrect notices and the checks underway without ruling out concerns that remain unresolved.
tasks.explanation: Перевод должен сохранять двойную границу: неизвестное не равно ни доказанному вреду, ни доказанной безопасности.

transfer.prompt: A museum emails membership renewals to already-paid members; payments are safe, but address matching is still under review. Draft a statement with a next-update commitment and answer a worried caller without inventing a completed investigation or a legal conclusion.
transfer.model: PROPOSED STATEMENT: We are sorry that renewal requests were sent to members who had already paid. We are withdrawing those incorrect requests; existing payments remain safe. Address matching is still under review, so we cannot yet confirm that every message reached the intended recipient. We will publish another update at noon tomorrow, even if the review is still underway. CALLER REPLY: I understand why you are concerned. Your payment is safe, but we have not yet confirmed where every message went. I cannot tell you that someone else saw it or rule that out. You can check the next update at noon tomorrow; we will distinguish confirmed findings from questions still being reviewed.
transfer.explanation: Новая ошибка требует собственного подтверждённого факта — платежи, а не блокировки.

units.reflectionPrompt: Перепиши публичное заявление и один ответ звонящему. По-русски объясни, где убрал излишнее успокоение, где избежал паники и как сделал следующее действие конкретным.

units.title: Создать критическое предисловие к архиву
units.why: Сделай самостоятельное прочтение сложного текста и его редакционной истории, сохраняя конкурирующие интерпретации и точную границу свидетельства.

materials.title: Письменные материалы
materials.text:
ARCHIVAL DOSSIER — original fictional material.
A private archive has acquired drafts of an essay by the late novelist Mara Vale, provisionally titled “The Uses of Silence.” The published 1987 version begins: “In our town, nobody was forbidden to speak. It was simply understood that sensible people had already said enough.” It later describes a meeting at which the narrator proposes repairing a footbridge. “The chairman thanked me for raising a matter so close to all our hearts and assigned it to a committee sufficiently distinguished to survive without meeting.” The essay never names the town or identifies a real council. In a surviving draft, the narrator calls the bridge “the route the factory women used before dawn”; the published version replaces this with “a route few officials had occasion to take.” The draft also ends with a direct question about who benefits when delay is praised as prudence. The published ending is less explicit: “By winter, we had achieved agreement on the importance of crossing. The river, unimpressed by procedure, continued to do so.”
A letter from Vale’s editor recommends removing “the local particulars that make a wider comedy look like a private quarrel.” A second letter, from Vale to a friend, says: “I have made it less indictable and perhaps less innocent. Whether that counts as improvement depends on who is reading.” The archive has no reply from the friend. The editor’s marked typescript is dated two weeks before a municipal election in Vale’s hometown, but no document states that the election motivated the revisions. A later interviewer asked Vale whether the essay attacked a particular mayor. She answered, “A reader who needs one mayor may keep one. I had a more durable office in mind.” In the same interview she said that she disliked having fiction “searched for concealed minutes of actual meetings.”
The archive plans a digital edition showing variants beside the published text. A family representative prefers an introduction emphasizing universal satire; a local historian argues that removing the factory women makes class and gender less visible. Both readings can draw on the texts, but neither settles why every change was made. The edition may quote the supplied passages in full because they are fictional materials created for this learning task. Your commission is a critical preface for attentive nonspecialist readers, accompanied by a brief editorial note. The preface should advance an interpretation rather than merely list possibilities. It must distinguish textual effects from historical motives, avoid treating the narrator as a transparent version of the author, and explain why the variants matter without implying that the earliest draft is automatically the most authentic. No additional historical evidence may be invented.

materials.title: Сообщение / разговор
materials.text: Editor: If the introduction leads with factory women, readers may treat the published essay as a censored political document. That is one story, but it is not established by the file. Historian: Agreed. Yet calling the revision “universal” can sound as though the people removed from the sentence were incidental clutter. They are not incidental to the draft’s account of who needs the bridge. Critic: Perhaps the change does two things at once. It reduces explicit social detail while making official indifference the sentence’s organizing contrast. That is a textual claim, not a claim about the editor’s private intentions. Family representative: Mara resisted being reduced to local feuds. Critic: She did, and her interview itself uses a joke to resist the question. But an author’s later account does not close every interpretive question about the work. Editor: What about “less indictable and perhaps less innocent”? It is irresistible. Historian: It is also ambiguous. “Less innocent” might mean subtler complicity, sharper satire or simply greater awareness of how readers assign blame. Critic: We should show why the phrase supports more than one emphasis, then explain which reading our preface finds most persuasive. Family representative: I can accept that if conjecture is labeled. What I would resist is a confident story in which the election explains everything merely because the dates happen to align. Editor: And readers should see that revision is not a ladder from truthful draft to compromised publication. The published ending gains an image of the river that the direct question did not have. Critic: Exactly. Loss and gain need not cancel each other, and neither needs to be hidden.
